statements.scope: For data from droplet and chamber-based digital PCR instruments, using the partition volume you declare. The positive and accepted partitions are the counts your instrument's software gives: this tool does not call partitions positive or negative, or set a threshold. Original sample: the material before the first dilution you entered, for example your vector lot or your DNA extract.
statements.researchUse: Research use only. Not qualified for GxP decision-making.
statements.citation: Modi, A.B. (2026). Digital PCR Calculator (v1.0.0) [Computer software]. Ligant AI Incorporated. benchtools.ligant.ai/digital-pcr-calculator/

precision.display: Results are shown to 7 significant figures, and lambda to 10, so that you can follow the arithmetic by hand. The number of digits is not the precision of the measurement, which this release does not calculate; the counts beside each result show how many partitions it rests on. Values of 10 million or more are written in scientific notation.
precision.rounding: The tool rounds to the digits shown only for display. Every later step uses the unrounded value, held at the computer's full precision of about 16 significant digits, which is a limit of the arithmetic, not of the measurement. Multiplying the shown values by hand can therefore differ from the result in the last digits.

constants.name: Poisson relation

constants.appliesTo: Every lambda

source.citation: Quan P-L, Sauzade M, Brouzes E. dPCR: A Technology Review. Sensors 2018;18(4):1271, section 2.1
quotes: the ratio of positive partitions k (containing some target sequences) over the total number of partitions n is sufficient to predict the initial concentration of the target sequence in the sample with λ=−ln(1− k/n).

constants.labelledAs: Ligant's mapping: k = positive partitions; n = accepted partitions.

constants.name: Copies per µL of reaction
constants.basis: Derivation: lambda is the mean number of copies per partition, and each partition holds Vd µL, so copies per µL of reaction = lambda ÷ Vd.
constants.appliesTo: Every copies per µL of reaction, and every value computed from it

constants.name: Template ratio
constants.basis: Derivation: the sample is mixed into the whole reaction, so the sample's concentration is the reaction's concentration times total ÷ sample.
constants.appliesTo: Each preparation's template ratio, and every value computed from it
constants.labelledAs: Ligant's reading: Addgene's titer protocol divides by the volume of virus in the reaction mix. Reading its R and V as the loaded volume and the sample in it gives 20 ÷ 4 = 25 ÷ 5 = 5, the same ratio as total ÷ sample.

constants.name: Dilution factor
constants.value: total ÷ volume in per step; product in bench order
constants.basis: Definition.
constants.appliesTo: Each dilution step's factor and each preparation's overall factor

constants.name: µL per mL
constants.basis: Unit definition.
constants.appliesTo: Every per-mL value

constants.name: Order of evaluation

constants.name: Expected accepted partitions, ratio limit, working range

constants.name: Mean of ticked wells
constants.value: Arithmetic mean of each ticked well's result, in listed order
constants.basis: It is not a result from the wells' counts added together.
constants.appliesTo: The mean of the ticked wells, per µL and per mL

constants.name: Limits
constants.value: 6 preparations per analysis; 8 wells and 6 steps per preparation
constants.basis: Product limits, not science.
constants.appliesTo: The whole analysis

constants.name: Displayed precision
constants.basis: Shown so that you can follow the arithmetic by hand.
constants.appliesTo: Every display string

constants.name: Rounding
constants.value: Half away from zero on the exact binary value, once, for display
constants.basis: No intermediate value is rounded to display precision; each is carried as a double.
constants.appliesTo: Every display string

constants.name: Lambda evaluation form
constants.value: −log1p(−p), the same quantity as −ln(1 − p), which the page writes
constants.basis: −log1p(−p) gives the same quantity as −ln(1 − p) and keeps its last digits when p is small. With 1 positive partition in 10,000,000, −ln(1 − p) is wrong in the 10th significant figure, a figure the page shows.
constants.appliesTo: Every lambda

constants.name: Agreement between implementations
constants.value: Displayed values, statuses, refusals, flags and labels identical; unrounded values within a relative difference of 1e-15
constants.basis: Tested for this engine version: an independent reimplementation and independently written expected values agree with this engine within this bound.
constants.appliesTo: Every result

assumptions.assumption: Partitions are of equal volume, the declared Vd, and targets are distributed among them at random.
The positive and accepted counts are from the same well and target, after your threshold.
The declared volumes are those pipetted.
The sample is uniformly mixed into the reaction, so the loaded or partitioned part has the reaction's concentration.
Every preparation in one analysis comes from the same original sample.
